lines.text: Gems were usually set in cups closed at the back.
Behind many stones went a thin sheet of metal foil.
Tinted copper foil deepened colored stones and silver foil brightened diamonds.
The closed cup held the foil in place and kept it safe.
At the Met, a garnet piece has pink foil to enhance color.
Foil under stones was meant to make them sparkle by candlelight.
But damp could ruin the foil and leave a dull look.
Later, open backs replaced foil, mostly in the 1800s.
lines.say: Later, open backs replaced foil, mostly in the eighteen hundreds.

post.caption: Georgian gems hid tinted foil underneath. Georgian jewelry in Britain dates from 1714 to the 1830s. Gems were usually set in cups closed at the back. Behind many stones went a thin sheet of metal foil. Tinted copper foil deepened colored stones and silver foil brightened diamonds. The closed cup held the foil in place and kept it safe. At the Met, a garnet piece has pink foil to enhance color. Foil under stones was meant to make them sparkle by candlelight. But damp could ruin the foil and leave a dull look. Later, open backs replaced foil, mostly in the 1800s.
